extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI): the user-controlled 'username' query parameter (source: main.py:8, read_root(username=None)) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string passed to Environment.from_string() and rendered at main.py:14. An attacker can inject Jinja2 template syntax, e.g. ?username={{ 7*7 }}, and achieve arbitrary code execution with payloads such as {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}. The commented-out 'safe implementation' on line 17 confirms the intended fix is to pass username as a template variable instead of concatenating it into the template source.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): the user-controlled 'username' query parameter is concatenated unescaped into the template rendered at main.py:14 (the Jinja2 Environment() at line 11 is created without autoescape=True), and the resulting output is returned to the browser with media type text/html via HTMLResponse(content=output). A payload such as ?username=<script>alert(1)</script> is reflected verbatim and executes in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
